checks.goodAnswer: A per-tenant-type table naming the instrument, standard, obligated party and contract clause, signed off by legal, with draft instruments clearly marked and an owner watching them. Contracts state the target (WCAG 2.2 AA), remediation SLAs and audit cost allocation, and we hand tenants an evidence pack that satisfies their verification duty.
checks.label: Legal applicability and allocation
probes: Which tenants are government bodies (GIGW, ADA Title II), SEBI-regulated entities or MIIs (SEBI circular of 31 July 2025), or private institutions (RPwD Act s.46 service providers), and is that recorded per tenant in tenant settings?
Does the master service agreement state the conformance target, who remediates, response times for accessibility defects, and who pays for third-party audits that a tenant's regulator requires?
Under the draft RPwD amendment, an establishment cannot rely on a supplier's ACR without due diligence. What evidence do we give tenants so their verification is quick and credible?
Which instruments are still draft or under litigation (draft RPwD amendment rules, EN 301 549 v4.1.1 harmonisation), who watches for final versions, and what is the trigger to update this node?
Has counsel confirmed whether the European Accessibility Act or US ADA Title III exposure exists for any tenant, rather than assuming it does or does not?
If a tenant demands a lower target than our platform standard (for example "WCAG 2.0 is enough"), can it opt out, and how is that prevented from reducing the platform for others?
checks.question: For each tenant type and region this surface serves, who is legally responsible for accessibility, under which instrument, and are those duties reflected in our contracts and in the tenant's obligations to its regulator?
redFlags: "Accessibility law doesn't apply to private B2B software" asserted without legal review.
No record of which tenants are SEBI-regulated or government bodies.
Contracts silent on accessibility, or promising full conformance we cannot evidence.
Draft rules treated as final, or final rules ignored.

refs.title: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (India Code)
SEBI: Compliance guidelines for digital accessibility (circular dated 31 July 2025)
Guidelines for Indian Government Websites and Apps (GIGW 3.0): scope

checks.goodAnswer: A versioned ACR where every row links to test evidence in the repository or test-management tool, a named qualified evaluator, a signatory, and a rule that a major release cannot ship without a refreshed ACR. Partial support and exceptions are described in terms of user impact with workarounds.
checks.label: Integrity of the conformance claim
probes: Is the claim scoped to named pages, states and versions, and does it include the states auditors find most failures in (errors, empty states, timeouts, modals)?
For each criterion marked "Supports", is there a stored test record (date, tester, method, AT used, build hash)?
How are "Partially supports" items described so a reader understands the real impact, rather than vague wording?
Is a third-party content exception (uploaded pleadings, tenant-supplied text) claimed, and is it the narrow, statement-based kind WCAG permits rather than a blanket excuse?
Who reviews the ACR before signature, and is there a rule that the ACR is re-issued after major UI changes?
Are AI-generated captions, alt text or summaries counted as conformant only after human review?
checks.question: Would our conformance claim for this surface survive an independent audit or a complaint to the Chief Commissioner, and is every statement in the ACR backed by test evidence?
redFlags: ACR filled in from automated scan results only.
"Supports" claimed for criteria never manually tested.
No version or date on the ACR, or one reused across products.
Machine-generated captions or alt text counted as conformant without review.

refs.title: ITI: Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT)
W3C WAI: WCAG-EM Overview (evaluation methodology)
W3C WAI: Conformance Evaluation and Reports

checks.goodAnswer: An inventory of tenant-configurable elements with the automated check applied to each and blocked activation on failure, no arbitrary CSS or script injection, and a per-tenant statement generated from the platform ACR plus tenant-specific exceptions. Ownership of tenant-supplied templates is set out in the contract.
checks.label: Tenant customisation and content
probes: Which tenant-configurable elements can affect accessibility: colours, fonts, logos, custom fields, form-builder forms, email and document templates, landing-page rich text, embedded third-party scripts?
Is each one validated at save time (contrast, labels, alt text, heading order), and what does the tenant admin see when it fails?
Can a tenant inject custom CSS or scripts? If so, how are focus styles, motion preferences and screen-reader behaviour protected?
Is a theme checked in both light and dark modes, high-contrast mode and at 400% zoom before activation?
Who owns remediation if a tenant's own uploaded document templates (for example an institution's award template) produce untagged PDFs?
Does each tenant's accessibility statement reflect that tenant's configuration and contacts, not a generic platform statement?
checks.question: Can any tenant configuration, branding, form, template or tenant-written content break conformance for that tenant's users, and what stops it?
redFlags: Tenant themes activated without contrast checks.
Form builder allows placeholder-only labels or inaccessible custom widgets.
Arbitrary tenant CSS or JavaScript allowed.
One generic accessibility statement for all tenants.

refs.title: W3C: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2

checks.goodAnswer: Build-blocking automated checks on components and journey states, keyboard end-to-end tests for each critical journey, accessibility criteria in the Definition of Done, severity-based defect SLAs with tracking, and a scheduled manual audit cycle with defined triggers.
checks.label: Preventing regression
probes: Which automated checks run on every pull request (axe on Storybook stories and journey states, lint rules such as jsx-a11y), and which severities fail the build?
Are accessibility acceptance criteria part of the Definition of Done for every UI ticket, and who checks them in review?
Is there a keyboard and focus-order end-to-end test for each critical journey (file, pay, accept appointment, submit award) in Playwright?
How are design-system component changes tested for downstream accessibility impact before release?
What is the defect SLA by severity (for example blocker: hotfix within 5 working days), and is it tracked on a dashboard?
How often is a full manual audit repeated, and what triggers an unscheduled one (new persona, major redesign, new AT version)?
checks.question: Once conformant, what stops this surface from falling out of conformance through ordinary releases, dependency upgrades or new features?
redFlags: Accessibility tested once before launch and never again.
Automated violations reported but never block the build.
No severity scheme or SLA for accessibility defects.
Component library changes shipped without accessibility review.

refs.title: W3C WAI: Accessibility Conformance Testing (ACT) Overview
W3C WAI: WCAG-EM Overview (evaluation methodology)

checks.goodAnswer: Every sign-in, step-up and KYC path is listed with its accessible method and a human-assisted fallback that does not make the user disclose more than needed. Liveness and video KYC have a documented alternative, guardian or representative flows exist, and these paths are in the AT test scripts.
checks.label: Authentication and identity verification
probes: Does every authentication path meet 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication: paste and password-manager support, no puzzle CAPTCHAs, passkey or magic-link options?
Do OTPs by SMS or email allow enough time and a resend, and is the time limit adjustable or long enough (2.2.1)?

Where video KYC or liveness checks are used, what alternative exists for blind users, users with facial differences or acid-attack survivors, as directed by the Supreme Court in Pragya Prasun v. Union of India (30 April 2025)?
Is any bot protection (for example a CAPTCHA provider) accessible, and what is the fallback when it fails?
Can a lawful guardian or authorised representative act for a person with a disability, as DPDP Act s.9 contemplates for consent, and is that relationship shown in the UI and audit trail?
Is step-up before consequential actions (submitting an award, changing bank details) accessible by the same standards?
checks.question: Can a person with any disability sign in, pass step-up checks and complete identity or KYC verification on this surface without help from another person?
redFlags: Image or audio CAPTCHA as the only bot check.
Liveness check with no alternative path.
OTP expires in under a minute with no extension.
Assisted sign-in that requires sharing credentials with a helper.

refs.title: W3C: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
W3C WAI: What's New in WCAG 2.2
Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (MeitY)

checks.goodAnswer: A defined accommodation workflow with timers and tribunal decision, accessible deadline display and reminders, a turnaround target for accessible copies of uploaded documents, and hearing features for interpreters and captions. Disability information is stored as sensitive data with restricted access.
checks.label: Equal participation in proceedings
probes: Can a user request an accommodation (accessible copy of a bundle, extra time, interpreter, CART) from within the case, and is the request routed to the tribunal secretary as a procedural request with a timer?

Are deadlines and time limits shown in ways that work with screen readers and cognitive disabilities (absolute date, time zone, plain countdown) and are reminders sent through the user's chosen accessible channel?
When an opposing party uploads an inaccessible document, how quickly can an accessible version be obtained and does the deadline account for the delay?
Do hearings support sign-language interpreter pinning, live captions in the hearing language, and keyboard control of the hearing room?
Are transcripts and recordings delivered in accessible formats within the same turnaround as for other users?
Is a record kept of accommodations granted, visible to the tribunal but protected as sensitive personal data?
checks.question: Can a party, counsel or neutral with a disability take part in the proceedings on equal terms, including meeting deadlines, reading the record and attending hearings?
redFlags: Accommodation handled informally by email with no record.
Deadlines that run while a party waits for an accessible copy.
Hearing room with no caption or interpreter support.
Disability details visible to opposing parties.

refs.title: W3C WAI: Making Audio and Video Media Accessible
Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (India Code)

checks.goodAnswer: A register of third-party components with dated ACRs and our own test results, accessibility in procurement and contract terms, a working alternative route for each critical vendor step, and periodic re-testing after vendor releases.
checks.label: Third-party and embedded components
probes: Is there a list of every embedded or redirected third-party component with its current ACR or VPAT and its date?
Has each been tested in our journey with our AT matrix, not only accepted on the vendor's word?
Is accessibility a procurement criterion and a contract term (conformance target, remediation SLA) for new vendors?
What is the fallback when a vendor component is inaccessible (for example a payment page that fails with screen readers): an alternative payment route, assisted payment, offline option?
Do third-party widgets obscure focus or trap keyboard users (2.4.11, 2.1.2)?
How are vendor regressions detected after their releases?
checks.question: Which third-party services appear inside this surface (video conferencing, e-signature, payment gateways, document viewers, chat or help widgets, KYC providers), and how is their accessibility assured?
redFlags: Vendor ACR accepted without our own testing.
No alternative when a payment or e-signature step is inaccessible.
Chat or cookie widgets that trap focus or hide focused content.
No accessibility terms in vendor contracts.

refs.title: ITI: Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT)

checks.goodAnswer: A cadence of research and testing with disabled participants with outcomes recorded, an accessible multi-channel grievance route with named owners and measured targets, complaints feeding the backlog, and trained support staff.
checks.label: People with disabilities in the loop
probes: When were people with disabilities last involved in research or testing for this surface, which disabilities were represented, and what changed as a result?
Is the feedback and grievance channel itself accessible, offered in more than one form, and staffed with a named nodal officer for regulated tenants?
What are the acknowledgement and resolution targets, and are they met (tracked monthly)?
Are complaints classified by criterion and fed into the exceptions register and backlog?
Are support and secretariat staff trained to assist users with disabilities, as SEBI's guidelines and the Pragya Prasun directions expect?
Are participants paid and is their personal data handled under the research consent process?
checks.question: How do people with disabilities shape and check this surface, and how are their complaints handled and learned from?
redFlags: No testing with disabled users at all.
Grievance route only through an inaccessible form.
Complaints closed without a fix or workaround.
Support staff with no accessibility training.
